subject: Human Evolution
title: The Recursion Debate
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Recursion Debate usable.

hook.text: You can say 'the cat the dog chased ran.' That sentence nests one clause inside another. That's recursion.

buildup.text: Chomsky argued recursion is human language's single unique feature—the one thing no animal has.

discovery.text: Recursion lets you build infinitely long sentences from finite rules. It's grammar's secret engine.

twist.text: The Pirahã people of Brazil may lack recursion in their grammar—challenging Chomsky's universal claim.

climax.text: Whether recursion is truly universal remains one of linguistics' fiercest ongoing debates.

punchline.text: One rule might separate human language from all else.

quiz.question: What is recursion in language?
options: Nesting clauses within clauses to build complex sentences
